subject: dec-concurrency-backend-framework
text: - **[Concurrency / Backend Framework] Hybrid sync core + Tokio only in `mcp` (KEYSTONE).** Rationale: portable-pty's handles are blocking, so the pump needs threads either way. `hook` spawns once per hook event and must not pay for runtime startup. rmcp and interprocess-async require Tokio, so it is confined to the subcommand that uses them. CI enforces this with a sole-root `cargo deny` `tokio` ban (`deny-sync.toml`, run once per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`), evaluated for the Windows, macOS and Linux target triples, plus a `cargo check` of the listed sync crates on all three OSes (CI job 3). `viola-channel`, whose optional `tokio` feature `viola-mcp` enables, is not on that list (since chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): its normal graph without the feature is proven tokio-free by `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` in the same CI supply-chain step.

subject: dec-pty
text:
- **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.8.1` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF, because ConPTY does not close the output stream on exit. If 0.8.1's Windows `kill()` misbehaves, the fallback is `TerminateProcess` on `child.process_id()` via windows-sys. The host stdin handed to the pump is `viola_pty::host_stdin()`: on Windows with a console stdin it is viola's own reader calling `ReadConsoleW` (no Ctrl-Z wakeup control; UTF-16 → UTF-8, a split surrogate carried, every `0x1A` kept, a 0-unit read read again), because std's console stdin drops a read's trailing `0x1A` and ends input on a lone `^Z` — source-read at the pinned toolchain and as measured on `windows-2025` (ci#37226294797, `tui_ctrl_z…` green); elsewhere, and for a redirected Windows stdin, it is `std::io::stdin()`. Its callers are `run`'s pump and the fake agent. Rationale: 0.8.1 is spike-proven (S1, O1 render stress, the Pulse live test, and about an hour driving this arch session in Windows Terminal with no PTY defect). 0.9.0 is excluded because of the Windows garbage-read bug wezterm#6783. Swap triggers: portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 if the O1 stray-spaces artifact reproduces only under `viola run` (then test `PASSTHROUGH_MODE`). An own ConPTY on windows-sys 0.61.2 + nix 0.31.3 comes only after a measured defect the seam cannot absorb. As built (chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows, measured on the Windows host in its research facts 1-5): `viola run` puts its own host terminal into raw input + VT output for the run through `HostTerminal` (Windows console modes; Unix termios) and restores the saved modes on Drop — without it ConPTY line-buffers keys until Enter and swallows Ctrl-C; off a terminal it is a no-op.
 The child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory (portable-pty 0.8.1 defaults to `%USERPROFILE%`). A revived start has the one other source: `viola revive` sets the child's cwd to the instance snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the directory the first start spawned its child in. It reads that value only after the strict-modes check on the instance's files, and it must name an existing directory, else the revive is refused `cwd-missing`. Program resolution and the version gate never read the recorded directory: the program is looked up on the reviving process's own `PATH`, from its own current directory (a boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-10, after it was shown to him as one, the overseer and the operator as relay; chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive). viola resolves the child program to an absolute path itself (portable-pty's Windows search tries the exact name first and hits the extensionless npm sh shim). The pump keeps the ConPTY input writer until the child exits, because dropping it makes conhost send `CTRL_CLOSE` to the child (exit `0xC000013A`). The exit is recorded as `exit_source` `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback`. As measured (chunk 2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe, H2): a key written through the seam right after `resize` returned can fail to reach the child — on the windows-2025 runner (image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260922.246.2), in an isolated loop of the viola-pty red test under `cargo llvm-cov nextest`, 13 of 200 iterations lost it (ci#36527891850), every loss the same class: the child's key-free size watcher saw the new size, viola's writer wrote and flushed the key, and the Rust test child blocked in its console read never received it; ConPTY wrote no cursor-position request (`dsr-cpr 0` on every loss, and on the dev host, Windows 10.0.26200.9457 / conhost 10.0.26100.8875, which read 20/20).
 The measured span runs from the ConPTY input-pipe write to that test child's console read; where inside it the key is lost is not established (an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source, relayed at that chunk's wrap, found no input-buffer flush on the resize path — a relay, not verified here). Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize is unmeasured; the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements" owns that measurement, blocked on an interactive Windows host (the harness's local `run --local-live`, a real-`claude` `viola verify`, does not claim it), and the founder's product question on H2 stays open. viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize ([Human Takeover / Wheel]). A test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first (0 of 200 lost, ci#36529038462). As built (chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty, founder ruling 2026-09-29): on Windows x64 the child's ConPTY is Microsoft's current one, sideloaded. Every `viola` process, in every role, restricts its DLL search to System32 as the second statement of `main` (`viola_pty::sideload::restrict_dll_search`, process-wide and one-way), so a bare-name load never picks a `conpty.dll` planted in the CWD or on `PATH`. `run` pins the embedded `conpty.dll` + `OpenConsole.exe` into `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` ([Deployment / Distribution]) and pre-loads `conpty.dll` by absolute path (`viola_pty::sideload::preload`: a relative path is refused, the module is never freed), so portable-pty `=0.8.1`'s own bare-name `LoadLibraryW("conpty.dll")` returns that module and the child is hosted by the pinned `OpenConsole.exe`; the seam and portable-pty are unchanged, and viola-pty knows no pinned path.
 `viola_pty::pty_backend()` reports `conpty-sideload` after a successful pre-load, else `conpty` (Windows) or `openpty`. An absent, tampered, unreadable or unloadable sideload fails open to kernel32's inbox ConPTY with no byte, refusal or exit change (`sideload_fallback` on `process-start`). Spawners outside `viola run` stay on the inbox ConPTY: the harness `supervise::spawn_in_pty`, root `tests/support/outer_pty.rs` and viola-pty's own tests. H2 with and without, measured in one run on the windows-2025 runner (image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587, ci#36563868040, the measurement-only race of the pre-`dce98ad` shape, 200 iterations each): sideloaded 0 of 200 lost, inbox 14 of 200 lost — beside the inbox 13 of 200 above; no rate is claimed. The sideloaded host writes a different spawn preamble, `ESC[1t ESC[c ESC[?1004h ESC[?9001h` (the inbox one: `ESC[?9001h ESC[?1004h`), and its DA1 query `ESC[c` holds the child's start until something answers it — as measured at the chunk's `evidence/da1-stall.md` on the dev host, 3.54 s unanswered on pipes vs 0.54 s answered (0.48 s on the inbox host); a terminal answers it, and the answer travels through viola's pump, so the child's start now waits for the pump. viola stays silent (it never answers DA1 itself); the stall of a `viola run` with no terminal on its stdio is an open product finding, owned by the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements", blocked on an interactive Windows host.

subject: dec-screen-model
text:
- **[Screen Model] vt100 0.16.2 as a pre-send readiness gate only.** After `turn-ended`, the gate waits for the screen to go quiet, then requires the absence of every known modal signature and waits, up to its maximum wait, for the version-stamped input-box signature. As landed, the model is the pure `viola_agent_claude::screen::Screen` (no I/O, no clock read; every instant is a parameter), and `run` feeds it on its own feed thread (`src/run/gate.rs`): a tee on the pump output writes the human's bytes first and then offers a copy with `try_send` into a queue bounded at `FEED_CAPACITY` = 256 messages (`sync_channel`; the pump copies at most 8192 bytes per write, so at most 2 MiB waits for the model), so the passthrough never waits on the model. The `Screen` sits behind a mutex shared by the feed thread and the `Gate` handle `send` reads (`Gate::wait_ready`, re-read every 20 ms); each feed and resize runs under `catch_unwind` inside that lock. A caught vt100 panic poisons the model until the host size changes, and so does a message the full queue drops (a dropped byte desynchronises the screen): one `parse-rejected{parser:"vt100-feed", detail:"oversize"}` per poisoning episode, and a size message carries the drop count at its offer, so a drop after a queued resize poisons the fresh screen again. A poisoned model reads `input-not-ready`. The quiet period (`QUIET_PERIOD` = 300 ms) and the maximum wait (`GATE_MAX_WAIT` = 8.5 s) are compiled built-ins in `viola-agent-claude`, validated per CLI version by the stamped `quiet-period` row (the ready and turn screens settle within `GATE_MAX_WAIT`). The maximum wait was 5 s until chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint raised it on the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-07T10:29Z (relayed by the overseer), so that it covers the CLI's 8.0 s paste hint ([CLI Version Compatibility]); the quiet period is unchanged.
 As measured on 2.1.287 at that chunk (`evidence/reverify-round.md`), the ready screen settled in 1 103 ms and the turn screen in 617 ms. The signatures are compiled in `viola_agent_claude::screen::SIGNATURES`: `input_box: ["for agents", "(shift+tab to cycle)"]` and `modals: ["Yes, I trust this folder", "Yes, allow external imports"]` (`Signatures::holds_any`). The second input-box literal is the resting footer a CLI keeps once it hides the first: on 2.1.302 the footer hint `for agents` is gone 15 s after the start and the row reads `⏵⏵ auto mode on (shift+tab to cycle)`, whose mode word is the user's permission mode, so the literal is the mode-independent `(shift+tab to cycle)`, which no other CLI text read holds (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/evidence/footer-2.1.302.md`). A screen is ready when a row contains an input-box literal and no row contains a modal literal. The per-version `modal-signature` row (an untrusted start shows a compiled modal literal) and `input-box-signature` row (the ready screen, the turn screen and the screen Run B settles on after the long paste's turn each hold an input-box literal and no modal; a long turn whose screen never settles fails it) validate them. They landed with chunk 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes, through the typed-input `viola verify` probe the founder ratified live on 2026-10-05 (relayed by the overseer), which runs the installed `claude` locally on the dev host only. `run` passes `Some(&SIGNATURES)` to `gate::start` exactly when its version gate read `cli_verified` (`Launched.cli_verified`): the full gate on a verified CLI version, and the partial gate otherwise. The verdict's consumer is confirmed `send`.
 On a verified CLI a modal row refuses at once, and a quiet screen with no input-box row keeps the gate waiting for one until `GATE_MAX_WAIT` has passed since the send entered the gate. A screen not quiet within the maximum wait, a poisoned model and a quiet screen still without an input-box row at the bound are refused: `send` types nothing and reports `not-delivered` with detail `input-not-ready`. The wait lives in the pure verdict (`Screen::verdict` reads `waiting_since`), so `Gate::wait_ready` did not change for it. Rationale: CLI-native modals bypass every hook (measured on 2.1.280: the "Teach auto mode…" modal swallowed a paste), and the screen lags the hooks. Signatures are compiled literals that each version's stamp validates. On a CLI version with no passing stamp the gate is partial: `Screen::verdict(None, …)` still refuses a poisoned model and a screen not quiet within the maximum wait, and a quiet screen is ready with no row read, so delivery confirmation decides the rest (the overseer's F1 reading of "falls back to delivery confirmation only", 2026-10-04). `Screen::rows()` is the only row-text exit, and only `viola verify` reads it. As measured at chunk 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes (research M13 and M19, the dev host's 2.1.288), the CLI's trust is inherited from a trusted parent folder. The external CLAUDE.md imports approval is keyed on the git root instead, so a subfolder of a repo whose import is unanswered shows "Allow external CLAUDE.md file imports?" until that answer is set. viola types into neither dialog.

subject: dec-delivery-confirmation
text:
- **[Delivery Confirmation] Every `send` is confirmed.** If no matching `prompt-submitted` arrives within the confirmation window, the send is reported as `not-delivered` with detail `no-prompt-submitted`. The confirmation window is the compiled `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` = 10 s in `viola_agent_claude::screen`, never in `config.json`; a `/compact` send waiting for its post-condition has its own, `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` = 40 s (PROVISIONAL, validated per CLI version by the `local-command-compact` row against the measured `compact_latency_ms`), and `SendSlot::window()` chooses the one bound that both `confirm`'s deadline and the `run.confirm_window` span's `window_ms` read. It is no longer provisional: the per-version `confirm-window` ledger row validates it (the typed prompt reaches UserPromptSubmit within the window, measured as `measured.typed_probe.prompt_latency_ms`), and `run` reads no window number from the stamp. `send` blocks for at most the readiness gate's maximum wait, plus the atomic paste, plus the window (18.5 s with the compiled 8.5 s and 10 s; 48.5 s plus the paste for a `/compact` send's 40 s window), and returns its result no later than when the window closes. On the MCP surface that total must stay below the MCP client's tool-call timeout, which on claude 2.1.287 exceeds 50 s (as measured live at chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), above the 48.5 s plus paste of a `/compact` send.
 Matching compares the typed text (the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters, below) with `prompt-submitted`'s `text` exactly (nothing else is trimmed), whatever `origin` the hook filed, `harness` included, after `viola-agent-claude` has normalised it: first the `<pasted_content id=…>` wrapper the CLI puts around long pastes is removed together with the frame the CLI writes around it (the two newlines directly before the open tag, the one directly after the close tag, and a second after it when text follows that is not the next pair's own frame), then the CLI's escaping of tag-like text is reversed (the landed `long-paste-wrapper` and `tag-escaping` rows). The wrapper-side matcher therefore never sees a Claude-specific shape, and a literal `<\pasted_content` the user typed is never mistaken for the wrapper. `send` types a text with every CR LF pair and every other CR inside it as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters (trailing LF: the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-07T15:21Z, relayed by the overseer, landed at chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed; trailing CR and CRLF: the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-09, relayed by the overseer, landed at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup; a CR or a CR LF inside a text, typed as the LF the CLI submits: the founder's ruling, live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-09T16:51Z, the options shown, relayed by the operator, landed at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text). `validate_paste_text` runs first, on the text as received.
 Directly after it the typed text is taken once (`viola_agent_claude::hook::typed_text`: every CR LF pair as one LF, every other CR as one LF, and every trailing CR and LF removed, in any order; it holds no CR, and nothing else changes, not a TAB, a space, or an LF that is not at the very end), and from there it is the only text `send` uses: the local-command classification, the in-flight text the match compares, `text_bytes` and the paste. A send whose text ends in one or more CR or LF characters (LF, CR, CRLF, or several of them) is therefore confirmed like any other: its `prompt-submitted` is relabelled `driver`, it ends `ok` `{submitted_at, cursor}`, and no `wheel` record is appended. The reason is a CLI behaviour (as measured on 2.1.287 on a verified and an unverified home at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/hint-window.md` step 7, `live-shape-red-green.md`): the CLI drops a pasted text's last newline before UserPromptSubmit, wrapped or not, so a text typed with it came back one byte short and the exact match failed. That measurement stands, and no `send` relies on it now. A text whose typed text is empty (the empty text, or a text of only CR and LF characters) is refused `not-delivered` / `empty-text` (exit 13) and is never issued: by the client before any frame (`refusal_of` in `src/cmd/send.rs`, the second product caller of `typed_text`, beside the wrapper's `send`) and by the wrapper directly after the typed text is taken and before the first wheel read, with nothing reserved, issued or typed, no cursor, and the wheel and the running-turn state not read (the founder's ruling, live, 2026-10-09, relayed by the overseer; landed at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup). This is proved under the fake agent, at the unit and cross-process layers on the three CI OSes.
 As measured on live `claude` 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`evidence/live-readings.ndjson`): a send ending in two newlines is typed without them (`text_bytes` 31 of 33 bytes sent), its prompt is filed `driver`, it is confirmed, and no `wheel` record follows. On that build, before chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup, a text of only newlines was issued with `text_bytes` 0, drew no `prompt-submitted`, and ended `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` (exit 13) when the window closed, with the wheel unmoved; and a text ending in one CR was typed with the CR (`text_bytes` 32), the CLI submitted it without the CR, the exact match failed, the prompt was filed `human`, the wheel moved to the human and the send ended `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` (exit 13). Both stand as records of the earlier build. As measured on live `claude` 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup (`evidence/live-run.md`, `evidence/live-readings.ndjson`): before the change, texts ending in CR LF and in CR CR were each submitted by the CLI without the whole ending, filed `human` and not confirmed (`trailing-crlf`, `trailing-cr-cr`); after it, texts ending in CR, CR LF and CR CR are each typed without the ending, filed `driver` and confirmed with no `wheel` record (`after-cr`, `after-crlf`, `after-cr-cr`), and a text of one CR LF is refused by the client, exit 13, `not-delivered` / `empty-text`, with no record in the wrapper (`after-empty-text`).
 Before chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text a CR or a CR LF inside a text was typed as it stood: the CLI submitted either as one LF, the typed text still held the CR, the exact match failed, the prompt was filed `human`, the wheel went to the human, the turn ended, and the send ended `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` (exit 13), so a delivered and answered driver text was reported not delivered and took the wheel from the driver (`after-inner-crlf`, `after-inner-cr`, as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup; both stand as records of the build before the rule). With the rule the typed text carries the LF itself, so a send whose text holds a CR or a CR LF inside is one paste of the typed text and is confirmed like any other, and no `send` types a CR or relies on what the CLI does with one. It is pinned under the fake agent at the unit tier and across processes, by reading the typed bytes. As measured on live `claude` 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text (`evidence/live-run.md`, `evidence/live-readings.ndjson`; one headless session of six sends, a local live measurement): texts holding one inner CR LF, one lone inner CR, two CRs in a row, an LF then a CR, and CR LF after two of three lines were each filed `driver` and confirmed with no `wheel` record and no CR in the submitted prompt (`rule-inner-crlf`, `rule-inner-cr`, `rule-inner-cr-cr`, `rule-inner-lf-cr`, `rule-crlf-lines`). The same session read first, as its control, that an LF typed inside a bracketed paste is submitted unchanged (`rule-inner-lf`).
 Every multi-line `send` relies on that shape, and it is gated by the ledger row `paste-newline` and its `viola verify` probe, Run B's `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` ([CLI Version Compatibility]), landed at chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row (the working-route entry "Paste newline ledger row", placed at the head of Epoch 5 on the founder's word, live in the overseer's dialog, 2026-10-09T20:58Z, relayed by the operator) and stamped on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host there (`evidence/live-round.md`: one prompt equal to the 113-byte text byte for byte). Not measured: any CLI version but 2.1.287, a long or wrapped multi-line text (every text was under 120 bytes and of at most three lines, the probe's 113-byte newline text included), an LF typed inside a paste on Windows (owed to "Windows-only live measurements"), and what the CLI does with a typed CR CR or LF CR (no `send` types one). As landed (the `send` module: `SendSlot::claim` / `settle` and `append_hook_event` in `src/run/send/slot.rs`), the wrapper claims the in-flight send's matching prompt, appends it with `origin:"driver"`, and only then settles the send with that line's `ts` as `submitted_at`, so `prompt-submitted` always precedes `send-confirmed` in `events.ndjson`. Skills are expanded into a prompt and fire UserPromptSubmit like any prompt (measured: `/andromeda-arch`), so a slash send that is not on the ledger's local-command list is an ordinary send, and if it is not confirmed the result is `not-delivered`. A built-in local command fires no UserPromptSubmit, so the ledger lists the known local commands, each with its post-condition or "none". If a listed command's measured post-condition is met, the send returns `ok`, confirmed.
 For `/clear`, that post-condition is a SessionStart with source `clear` and a new `session_id`; for `/compact`, a SessionStart with source `compact` and the session's own `session_id`. If a listed command's post-condition is "none" or not yet measured on this CLI version (`/remote-control` today), the send returns `ok` with `{"confirmed":false,"detail":"unconfirmable"}`. Nothing else is ever unconfirmable. Any other unconfirmed send is `not-delivered`. The decision depends on the ledger, never on a leading slash. The local-command list and the `/clear` row are compiled (`viola_agent_claude::ledger::LOCAL_COMMANDS`: `/clear` with the post-condition "a new session", `/remote-control` with none, `/compact` with "a SessionStart with source `compact` and the session's own `session_id`" (`PostCondition::CompactedSession`; listed since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows on the founder's own answer to its P4 fork 1, relayed verbatim by the operator; row `local-command-compact`); row `local-command-clear`, stamped on 2.1.287 by chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows through the ratified typed-input probe), and `send` consumes them (as landed by chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes; the decision is `classify` in `src/run/send/classify.rs`). When the send's slot is reserved the typed text is classified by exact equality with a list entry: nothing else trimmed, no case folding, never a leading-slash test.
 A listed command followed by newlines is therefore that command: `/clear` and a newline is `/clear`, and since chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup so is `/clear` and a CR or a CRLF (the LF consequence widened by the CR strip, pinned at the unit layer) (the founder was shown the LF consequence with the 2026-10-07 ruling above; proved at the unit layer, and as measured live on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive, `evidence/live-readings.ndjson`, `clear-then-newline`: `/clear` and one LF, `text_bytes` 6, confirmed by a new session of cause `clear`, no `prompt-submitted`, no `wheel` record). Every refusal rung applies to a listed command as to any text. A listed command whose post-condition is "none", and any listed command on a CLI version that is not verified (`/remote-control` on every version, `/clear` and `/compact` with no passing stamp), is typed and answered `unconfirmable` at once: `send-issued`, the paste, then the record `send-confirmed {cursor, confirmed:false}` and the `ok`, with no confirmation window. The verified bit is the version gate's `cli_verified`, handed to `SendSlot::new`; the send path reads no `ledger/stamps.json`. `/clear` on a verified version waits the window for its post-condition only, and no `prompt-submitted` claims it. The hook tap claims it on a `session-start` whose `cause` is `clear` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string that differs from the id the send slot remembers, appends that line unchanged, and only then settles the send with that line's `ts` as `submitted_at`, so the `session-start` precedes `send-confirmed`. The remembered id is the `agent_session_id` of the last `session-start` the tap took, whatever its cause, kept in memory under the in-flight send's lock: a line with no string id clears it, with nothing remembered any string id is new to the `/clear` claim, and nothing persists it.
 If the window closes first the send is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` with its cursor (no new detail). `/compact` on a verified version waits its own window for its post-condition only, and no `prompt-submitted` claims it: the tap claims it on a `session-start` whose `cause` is `compact` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string EQUAL to the id remembered before that line (read before the line replaces it), appends the line unchanged and settles as for `/clear`; another cause, another id, no string id, or nothing remembered claims nothing (with nothing remembered nothing equals it), and the send then expires at 40 s as `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted` with its cursor. The opening sentences of this entry, and the prompt claim, describe a send that is not a listed command. The `/clear` confirmation is proven on the recorded 2.1.287 `clear-1` variants replayed by the fake agent; against a live CLI it is as measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`evidence/live-run.ndjson`, its `clear` line): a driver `/clear` was confirmed by a `session-start` with cause `clear` and a new `agent_session_id`, with no `prompt-submitted`, and the next skill was sent into the cleared session. The `/compact` confirmation is proven on the recorded 2.1.287 `compact-1` variant, replayed by the fake agent under the session's own id; against a live CLI its post-condition is as measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host by `viola verify`'s Run B at chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row (`evidence/live-round.md`: a SessionStart of source `compact` under Run B's first id, read 21 413 ms after the paste); no live driver `send` of `/compact` has been made. Rationale: a turn boundary per the hooks does not prove the input box is ready. Confirmation is the backstop behind the screen gate.
 Local commands would otherwise be false negatives (measured: `/remote-control` fired no UserPromptSubmit), and `/clear` matters most because drivers clear between pipeline skills.

subject: dec-database-state-store
text:
- **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs because append + exclusive lock fails on Windows (rust-lang/rust#54118). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

subject: dec-snapshot-writer
text:
- **[Snapshot writer] tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` through ONE shared helper.** `viola_state::fs::replace_private` creates the temp file beside the target, sets its mode before any byte is written (0600, or 0700 for the pinned `viola`), writes, `sync_all`s and `persist`s; a failure leaves the target as it was. On Windows a `persist` refused with raw OS error 5 (a reader holding the target open, as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M1 under every share mode) is retried every 10 ms, re-persisting the same temp file, at most `viola_state::fs::REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` = 100 attempts (an attempt count, never a time bound); any other error returns at once. The loop sits in the private `replace_private_retrying`, which takes the decision to retry a failed rename (from its raw OS error) from its caller; `replace_private_with` passes `retry_replace(_, HOST_IS_WINDOWS)`, so the product's behaviour is the one above and the loop's attempt bound is exercised by a unit case on every host (chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors). `replace_private_shared` is the variant for files every concurrent start of one version writes identically (the pinned copy, the plugin files, the Windows x64 ConPTY companions under `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/`): a replace that fails counts as done when the target already holds exactly those bytes. The companions' held open (`FILE_SHARE_READ` only) retries a Win32 error 32 (sharing violation) under the same `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` bound (`retry_open`, `open_held_waiting`), as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty: two concurrent first starts, the refusal lasting 5-11 ms after the other start's write, 0 of 6 pairs over companions already written. No call site carries its own temp + rename code.
 Rationale: atomic-write-file 0.3.1 was the first choice, but its licence is BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`'s allow list (operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan); tempfile was already locked, MIT OR Apache-2.0.

subject: dec-message-broker-ipc
text:
- **[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.** `hook` blocks on the channel for a dialog answer. `wait` blocks until the next driver-relevant event (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` or `dialog-expired`) and returns that event, so nothing polls and a driver parked in `wait` learns that a dialog is pending. If a dialog is already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, it returns that dialog at once (as landed by 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: `hook.dialog` is served, the dialog line is appended and signalled through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` and cleared through `WaitFeed::dialog_settled`). With an `after` past that line the driver has already seen the dialog, so `wait` blocks for the next driver-relevant event, and a driver that leaves a dialog to the human never spins. Each dialog event carries a wrapper-assigned `dialog_id` (an integer, monotonic per instance, with the counter restored from `events.ndjson` on start so an id never repeats across wrapper restarts), and `answer` names its target by that id. At most one dialog is pending per instance. A `hook.dialog` that arrives while another is pending is answered `null` at once, so that dialog renders for the human. Its event is still logged with its own `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. Whether Claude Code can hold two dialog hooks open at once (for example on parallel tool calls) is a capability-ledger row. `wait` takes an optional `after` cursor and an optional `timeout_ms`. `after` is a byte offset into the instance's `events.ndjson`.
 `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it, at once if that event is already logged, so a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`, the offset to pass as the next `after`. Without `after`, `wait` returns the next such event appended after the call. With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until an event arrives, and if the endpoint vanishes first the caller gets `instance-unreachable`. On timeout it returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}`. `last` returns the `last_assistant_message` of the newest `turn-ended` event. The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start. Endpoint names are a short hash of the instance, never the raw `VIOLA_NAME` + path. On Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, adopted by `Stream::try_from`), never interprocess's default connect, so a squatted or rogue server cannot impersonate the client; a non-overlapped handle adopted this way hangs (as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites). Rationale: one API over named pipes and Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. macOS caps socket paths at about 104 bytes. Accepted risk: interprocess has one main maintainer, which the seam contains.

Every frame-writing client compares that pid and the process's OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame (§Standard Contracts, Channel methods), so on Linux and Windows a squatted or rogue server is never sent a frame either.

subject: dec-mcp
text:
- **[MCP] rmcp 3.4.1, stdio, tools `send · wait · last · answer · list`. `release` is CLI-only.** Refusals are `isError: true` tool results mapped from `result.refusal`. Rationale: it is the official SDK, tracks spec 2026-07-28, and the pinned minor limits churn from its near-weekly releases. `answer` and `list` are how a driver answers dialogs under R7 and sees sessions, and the prototype driver uses both every session. `release` stays off the driver's tool surface, so a driver is never offered a way to hand the wheel back to automation. This is an affordance, not an enforcement: an agent's Bash tool can still run CLI `viola release` (for example through `VIOLA_BIN`), and the Local endpoint trust boundary accepts it because v1 trusts every process of the same OS user. The wrapper refuses a `release` whose `params` carry a string `from` (`-32602`, `data.reason` `release-from-driver`), so CLI `viola release` run inside a wrapped session (`VIOLA_NAME` set) is refused; `from` is self-reported (`from_trust:"self-reported"`), so this deters rather than enforces. `pause`, `link` and `unlink` are CLI-only for the same reason: they are human controls over the wheel and the link topology, and links made by drivers are already recorded from `from` on `send` and `answer`. Tool inputs:
  - `send {target, text}`
  - `wait {target, after?, timeout_ms?}`
  - `last {target}`
  - `answer {target, dialog_id, response}`, with `response` in the channel `answer` shape
  - `list {}`

  `target` is a `ViolaName`, and the server adds `from` from its own `VIOLA_NAME` only when it has a name of its own. As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler takes the raw argument object and re-validates it, a schema violation being the `invalid-params` result with a closed field `detail` and no frame (§Conventions, Error handling schema), and an internal handler fault being the JSON-RPC error `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`; MCP `wait` sends `timeout_ms` = `min(given, 50 000)` (`viola_mcp::WAIT_CAP`, `wait_timeout`), 50 000 ms when none is given, and `after` as given. The bound sits below claude 2.1.287's stdio tool-call default, which exceeds 50 s (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 2: a default `wait` answered `timed-out` at 50 012 ms with no client timeout; the exact default is unmeasured). `list` builds the CLI's board and makes its one `claude agents --json` read (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness; the founder's own answer, that chunk's `inputs#I2` Q1).

subject: dec-hook-transport
text:
- **[Hook Transport] Exec-form `command` hooks: `"command": "<pinned viola copy>", "args": ["hook", "<event>"]`.** Tiers:
  - sync with a decision: PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, plus PermissionRequest.
  - sync with no reply body (the ordering spine): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop. Each writes its `hook.event` and exits 0 within viola's spine deadline: one built-in value for every event, below the `timeout` (5 s) those hooks get in `hooks.json`. That value is the product constant `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s, the bound the perf gate reads (test-plan §10). The connect deadline `viola hook` passes to `Client::connect_by` is the hook-local, crate-private `CONNECT_DEADLINE` = 750 ms (provisional), asserted below `SPINE_DEADLINE` by a unit test. If the endpoint cannot be reached or written within the deadline, the hook records the failure in `diagnostics/` and exits 0. The event is lost rather than the turn delayed, and a driver recovers through `wait`'s `timeout_ms`.
  - SessionEnd: sync within viola's own ~1 s budget: the channel under the same provisional 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, else, when the endpoint is not reached or its server check fails, a direct `try_lock` append (`viola_state::try_append_event` with `Source::Hook`, which writes nothing while `events.ndjson.lock` is held), else nothing; `hooks.json` gives it no `timeout` key. `run` writes `session-end` from the process exit if no hook arrived.
  - `async: true`, printing nothing: Notification, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure.

  Rationale: exec form skips Git Bash path rewriting and shell startup. `http` hooks need a fixed URL, which means a central listener and so a daemon. `mcp_tool` is unavailable at SessionStart. The 1.5 s SessionEnd budget is never raised. The tier map is itself a ledger row that `viola verify` re-stamps.

subject: dec-hook-transport
text: - The event and dialog paths share one connect: `read_snapshot`, then `Client::connect_by`, then `verify_server` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). A serving process whose pid or OS start time is not the snapshot's, or a check that cannot be made, gets no frame: the hook records `server-verify-failed` and exits 0 with no body, the event lost as for an unreachable endpoint.

subject: dec-hook-contract
text:
- **[Hook Contract] Hooks fail open.** Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision. Exit 0 with no body is no decision (the `unverified-cli` degrade: the dialog renders for the human). Exit 2 is never produced. `hook` exits 0 at once when `VIOLA_NAME` is absent. The one exception is the hidden `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]` arm, which only `viola verify`'s probe plugins call, and its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]`, which only Run B's probe settings call (it files the payload as `StatusLine.<k>.json` under the same claim and write, beside `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holding exactly `bin-sh` when the word equals `/bin/sh` byte for byte, else `other`, the word itself written nowhere; nothing printed; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, «Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`): it reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel; it takes an absolute, existing `<DIR>`, reads stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and claims `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json` exclusively — create-new at 0600 (`viola_state::fs::create_private_new`) from the first free `k`, the next `k` on `AlreadyExists`, then the raw bytes through `replace_private` over its own claim, so two concurrent captures never share a name (`k` counts across events, so names sort in arrival order). `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture` (inert without it): for a dialog event, the event's ordinal `j` in claim order selects `<DIR>/<Event>.<j>`, read through `take(64)` as an exact closed `ProbeAnswer` id, and `ledger::probe_body` builds the body from the filed payload through `dialog::decision_body` alone — one write to stdout, the probe's dialogs answered by the hook, never by a key.
 Any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0 (the capture arm a boundary widening ratified live by the founder, 2026-09-28 20:24:32; its `--answers` body the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer). A sync dialog hook (`viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request`) waits on `hook.dialog` for at most the instance's dialog hold, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`: whole seconds from 60 to 3600, default 60 (`viola_core::DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX`, PROVISIONAL, beside `SPINE_DEADLINE`), a `DialogHold` read once at the wrapper's start; the hook bounds its reply read at the ceiling, `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s), never at each start's hold, and writes stdout once. The dialog hooks' `timeout` in the embedded `hooks.json` is 3615 s, above the ceiling by a margin a test pins, so viola, never Claude Code, ends the wait, and the rendered plugin stays byte-identical across starts. At the hold's end the wrapper replies `null`: the hook exits 0 with no body and the dialog renders for the human. The wrapper then clears the pending `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. `hook` never writes to stderr. Its codes-only process log goes to the home-level `diagnostics/hook-<name>.ndjson`, and content-bearing detail goes only to the instance's `diagnostics/detail-hook.ndjson` (format owned by obs). A failure to write either is ignored. Rationale: exit 2 is a blocking error in Claude Code's contract, and a viola bug must never block the user's session.

subject: dec-human-takeover-wheel
text:
- **[Human Takeover / Wheel] Byte-source claim + atomic send window + after-the-fact confirmation, explicit release.** Any human editing key since the last turn boundary moves the wheel to the human, and `send` is refused with `human-typing`. Only a closed non-editing list never counts (the founder's live ruling F-W2, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer): focus reports (`CSI I` / `CSI O`), mouse reports (X10 `CSI M` + 3 bytes, SGR `CSI < n;n;n M|m`, urxvt `CSI n;n;n M`) and terminal replies (DA1 `CSI ? … c`, DA2 `CSI > … c`, CPR `CSI n;n R`, DECRPM `CSI ? n;n $ y`, kitty flags `CSI ? n u`, OSC replies ending BEL or ST, DCS replies ending ST, and seven further reply shapes, each after `CSI` by exact grammar, the fields compared as bytes, no intermediate byte and the field count exact: DSR status `CSI 0 n`, colour scheme `CSI ? 997;1 n` and `CSI ? 997;2 n`, window size `CSI 4;n;n t`, cell size `CSI 6;n;n t`, text area `CSI 8;n;n t`, in-band resize `CSI 48;n;n;n;n t`, modifyOtherKeys reply `CSI > 4;n m`); a host resize is no stdin byte at all. The seven joined the list at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive, ratified by the founder himself on 2026-10-08 after the exact grammars and a narrower option of two were shown (relayed verbatim by the overseer). As measured on foot 1.28.0 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/terminal-replies.md`, `evidence/reply-probe.ndjson`, `evidence/reply-probe-fixed.ndjson`): before, those seven replies of the terminal were read as typing, and a live `claude` 2.1.287 took the wheel from the driver 237 ms after it started with no key typed; after, none of 23 probe queries is read as typing, and the nearest human keys (`n`, `t`, `m`, their Alt forms, their kitty key events) and a sequence one field or one prefix away from a listed shape still take the wheel.
 A reply no terminal has been measured to write is not added on a guess. Every other byte takes the wheel: ground bytes, every other completed sequence, a sequence past 64 bytes of parameters or payload, and a C0 inside a sequence (which aborts it). A read ending on a lone ESC is the Esc key at once, and a sequence past `ESC [` / `ESC ]` / `ESC P` / `CSI M` carries across reads. The classifier only observes: the stdin observer (`run::wheel::Observed`, wrapping the host stdin handed to `viola_pty::pump_with_paste`) returns every byte whole and unchanged, and a read holding an editing key moves the wheel before it returns.
 On Windows the platform decides what arrives (the founder's live ruling F-W3, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer): the inbox ConPTY outer terminal swallows focus reports, and under the sideloaded ConPTY's win32-input-mode request (`ESC[?9001h`) a mouse report written as text into the console's input arrives as one win32 key-down record per character (`ESC[0;0;<Uc>;1;0;1_`) and takes the wheel — as measured on `windows-2025` (ci#37227518624) for injected bytes; a mouse report from a real Windows terminal is not yet measured. The error only ever favours the human. A bridge send is written as one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR write. Human bytes arriving during that write are held in the pump and passed on straight after. An unsent `prompt-submitted` confirms and logs the take: one the hook filed `origin:"human"` moves the wheel before its line is appended (a `harness` prompt and the relabelled in-flight `driver` prompt never move it). An in-flight send whose text ends in CR or LF characters is typed without them, and one whose text holds a CR or a CR LF inside is typed with each as one LF, so its own prompt matches, is relabelled `driver` and moves no wheel (as landed at chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed for LF, at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup for CR and CRLF at the end, and at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text for a CR or a CR LF inside; [Delivery Confirmation]). A prompt that is not the in-flight send's typed text claims nothing and is appended as the hook filed it, so one filed `human` still moves the wheel.
 Harness-injected prompts are classified as harness turns, never as a human take: a prompt whose raw start (no trim) is one of `viola-agent-claude`'s four compiled `HARNESS_PREFIXES` — `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message` or `<cross-session-message` (another Claude session's message; the unescaped form is the one measured from the CLI on 2.1.287, the escaped form is relayed and kept compiled, see Tag escaping). The side effect was accepted with the widening (the founder, live, 2026-09-29 15:21:44): a human who types the cross-session tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness`. As measured on 2.1.287, and not a new ratification, a human who types `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too. The wheel starts with `driver` when `viola run` starts, so automation is accepted until the first human editing key. A `send` while a turn is running (after `prompt-submitted`, before `turn-ended`) is not queued. It is refused `not-delivered` with detail `turn-running`, and the driver calls `wait` first. A `send` that arrives while another `send` is in flight (accepted, its outcome not yet recorded) is refused the same way, never queued, and nothing is typed for it. A `prompt-submitted` of any origin marks a turn running, and `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it. A turn can end with no `turn-ended`: Claude Code's Stop hook does not fire on a user interrupt, and which hook, if any, fires for a turn that ends on an API error is a ledger row (if one does, `viola-agent-claude` registers it and maps it to `turn-ended` with a `null` `last_assistant_message`). A human interrupt is human input, so it moves the wheel to the human, and the `viola release` that returns the wheel clears the running-turn state.
 As built (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal), the running-turn state lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside the holder and cause, and records no event, snapshot field, span or obs line, so a restarted wrapper starts with no turn. The wrapper's one hook entry (`run::send::append_hook_event`) marks it before the hook's line is appended, keyed on the line's kind alone: a `prompt-submitted` of any origin (the claimed driver prompt included) marks it running, `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it, and `activity` leaves it. So a driver that read `turn-ended` through `wait` is never refused by that turn. The turn is marked ahead of a human prompt's wheel move, so a `release` landing between the two still clears it. `send` reads the wheel and then the running turn twice, in that order both times: at the send's arrival, and again once the readiness gate's wait (up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, 8.5 s) has returned ready. A human key or a turn that started during the wait is refused `human-typing` or `not-delivered` / `turn-running`, with no `send-issued` and nothing typed (the overseer's technical answer of 2026-10-07T12:10Z at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, listed for the founder as a fact; it retires the residual recorded on 2026-10-04, under which a turn starting during the wait was not refused). The wait is not interrupted when the wheel moves: `Gate` knows nothing of the wheel, so the driver hears the refusal when the wait ends. Only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears the turn, in the same lock hold as the move. A `release` on a wheel the driver already holds, `release --budget` and a refused `release` (`release-from-driver`, invalid params) leave it, as do `pause` and human keys, so a turn left running under a driver-held wheel is recovered without a keystroke by `viola pause` then `viola release`.
 An unsent human prompt moves the wheel before its line is appended, so the `send` after it reads `human-typing`, never `turn-running`, and the `release` that returns the wheel also clears that turn. `release` never empties the in-flight `send` slot, which belongs to a live send. A SessionEnd the hook appends directly (the channel did not take it) leaves the turn marked — a recorded residual; its child is ending, so no driver `send` depends on it. A driver parked in `wait` across such a turn recovers through `timeout_ms`. CLI `viola pause` moves the wheel to the human without a keystroke, after which automated `send` is refused `human-typing` with detail `manual-pause`. The wheel returns only through CLI `viola release`; a `release` on a wheel the driver already holds changes nothing and appends nothing. The wheel lives in `src/run/wheel.rs` (`WheelSlot`: holder, cause and the running turn under one lock). The in-memory move is synchronous; each change's `wheel` event (`{holder, cause}`, `source:"wrapper"`, log-only, never through the wait feed), its snapshot update, its `run.wheel_transition` span and the pending-dialog hand-back run on the wheel's own worker thread, and `viola run` flushes that worker (bounded 2 s) at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode. Every snapshot write goes through the one in-process holder `src/run/snapshot.rs` (`Snapshots`). While the wheel is `human`, the wrapper answers `hook.dialog` with `null` at once, so the dialog renders for the human without waiting out the dialog hold, and `answer` is refused `human-typing`. If the wheel moves to the human while a `hook.dialog` is already pending (a human editing key or `viola pause`), the wrapper answers that pending request with `null` at once and clears its `dialog_id`, so a dialog held by the hook is never hidden from the human for the rest of the hold.
 `budget-paused` gates only `send`, never `hook.dialog` or `answer`, because a running turn finishes. Rationale: `viola run` owns the real stdin, so it knows byte provenance exactly. The prototype paused twice on harness turns before the classifier was fixed.

subject: dec-links
text:
- **[Links] A link `driver → driven` is recorded when a `send` or `answer` is issued from inside a wrapped session to another instance, or by an explicit `viola link <driver> <driven>`. `viola unlink` removes it.** A call counts as coming from inside a wrapped session when the calling process has `VIOLA_NAME` set. The CLI and the MCP server pass that name as `from` in the request `params`, and the driven instance's wrapper appends a `link` event to its `events.ndjson` only when that `driver → driven` pair is not already in its link set. Repeated sends and answers add no line, and an explicit `viola link` of an existing pair adds none and answers its held `since` with `already_linked: true` (§Standard Contracts, Instance snapshot), so `since` is the time of the first link after any `unlink`. `unlink` appends an `unlink` event. Links are events in the log. The link set in the snapshot is derived by replaying them. Rationale: the log stays the single source of truth for the link set as it is for everything else. Both are built: the driven instance's wrapper serves the `link` and `unlink` methods (`LinkSet::link` / `LinkSet::unlink`, sharing `driver_of`), sent by the verbs `viola link <driver> <driven> [--json]` and `viola unlink <driver> <driven> [--json]`, and records the implicit link itself. The driven wrapper's `LinkSet` (`src/run/links.rs`) records it on a `send` after the second wheel and running-turn reads and directly before `send-issued`, and on an `answer` once every refusal has passed and the response's kind matched the pending dialog, before the answer is taken. Five shapes of it stand on the operator's word and are not ruled by the founder: a refused `send` or `answer` records no link; a `from` equal to the wrapper's own name links nothing; the `link` line's `source` is `wrapper`; the record sits directly before `send-issued`, so a send that is issued and then reads `not-delivered` has linked; and a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`. A link that cannot be recorded is `-32603`, with nothing issued or the answer not taken. The set is restored from the log at every start.

subject: dec-budget-governor
text:
- **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused with `budget-paused` through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human keys are never blocked, and a running turn finishes. The pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`. `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is, and a plain `release` returns the wheel to `driver` without lifting a budget pause. `release --budget` is sent to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only, until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under `budget.json.lock`, at three points: at start, when a `send` arrives, and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of these points, and only then is `budget-gate` appended. So a snapshot can still read `budget_paused: true` after the reset, until a `send` arrives or a turn ends, and every surface that shows the snapshot inherits that. The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, including any override, to the instance snapshot, where `list` reads it. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `src/run/budget.rs`, one `BudgetGate` per wrapper, no thread and no timer): a window is crossed only when its `used_percentage` is known and at or above its threshold and its `resets_at` is known, parses as RFC 3339 and is later than now, so a window whose `resets_at` is `"unknown"`, unparseable or passed never pauses. With both windows crossed the refusal names `five-hour`.
 The `send` point sits after the text refusals and the first `human-typing` read and before the running-turn read, so the order is `control-character` → `empty-text` → `human-typing` → `budget-paused` → `turn-running` → the readiness gate's wait; the gate is read once per `send`, never again after that wait. `answer`, `wait`, `last`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` do not read the gate (read in the diff: its five product call sites; since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the root case `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`, `tests/cli_budget.rs`, drives `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under one closed gate, each giving the exit code and the document it gives under an open one; no case drives `hook.dialog` under a closed gate). An override covers both windows until its end and is dropped at the next point after that end. It does not outlive its wrapper: every start, a revived one included, evaluates from `budget.json` alone and restores none. `release --budget` with no pause standing records nothing. `budget-gate` is appended, and the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are rewritten, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, both before the evaluation returns; a record that cannot land is an error and the recorded state stays as it was. The thresholds are read once, at the wrapper's start, and no value of either switches the gate off. The gate is fail-open: no reading, an `"unknown"` figure, a passed or unparseable `resets_at`, an unreadable or refused `budget.json` and a bad threshold each leave it open or at its default. The decision takes the wall-clock instant as an argument (no clock seam). With figures missing, viola uses the newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age. With no reading at all it records `unknown` and does not block.
 The statusline is wrapped only for sessions started by `viola run`, through a per-session settings override that then runs the user's own statusline command unchanged. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through) the wrap is Unix only: on Windows no override is written and no command is run, and that half is owed to the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements" (the founder's word on the cut, live, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the operator). A reading is recorded only when the payload holds `rate_limits`. Rationale: the per-model weekly window is hidden (claude-code#91920), so thresholds are set low. The user's global statusline config is never touched, and a visible, conservative governor supports the "ordinary individual usage" posture.

subject: dec-session-liveness
text:
- **[Session Liveness] Heartbeat file primary; pid + process start time decide `gone`, and `claude agents --json` only enriches it.** Rationale: the prototype's heartbeat proved reliable. A bare pid is unsafe because pids get reused, which is why start time is matched too: a snapshot whose pid is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the heartbeat says (Session liveness). `claude agents --json` adds idle/busy status and shows unwrapped sessions as read-only rows. A `viola run` whose `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` refuses to start (exit 1, with a message naming the instance); once the endpoint exists, a name with an answering endpoint refuses the same way. `viola revive` refuses a `live` or `stale` name through the same collision check and its two stderr pairs, as the first of its four preflight readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory; a later reading is not taken once an earlier one refuses). `session-live` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips the reading, and a failed read passes (fail open). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (that chunk's `evidence/live-p4.md`), a second interactive `claude --resume <id>` of an id a live `claude` holds is neither refused nor copied: both sessions run under the one id, two writers on one transcript, so the reading stays a refusal; and after `/clear` the agents row of the session's pid names the new id (P12 follows), so a session-id join survives a `/clear` because the wrapper rewrites the snapshot's `agent_session_id` on each `session-start`. The strict-modes check on the home and the instance's files runs ahead of them, before the wrapper log opens (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor).
 A revive that passes goes through the same start as `run`, so the collision check runs twice. It resumes the `gone` instance in place: its `events.ndjson` is appended to with the earlier bytes unchanged, no launch is replayed, and its first record is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`, as every start's (the founder's answer, live, 2026-10-10, relayed by the operator: a revived start keeps the wheel at `driver`). Otherwise `run` starts in this order: program resolution (the `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal, which writes nothing), collision check, pinned copy and plugin folder, the ConPTY sideload (Windows x64, fail-open), version gate, exclusive bind of the endpoint (a bind that finds the name taken is an exit-1 refusal, `squatted-name`, so two concurrent starts cannot both win), first snapshot (with `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, and `statusline_command` when the named source gave a command; `pid`, `started_at`) and heartbeat, the start `wheel` and `budget-gate` events, then the child spawn, after which the snapshot is rewritten with `child_pid`. Between the first snapshot and the spawn `run` also rewrites the per-session settings override (Unix only; §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names).
 As landed by 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify every step has its place (the sideload step added by 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty): program resolution → collision → pinned copy and plugin → ConPTY sideload (`run.conpty_sideload`, Windows: `pin_companions` + the absolute-path pre-load; `outcome` `loaded` · `hash-mismatch` · `unreadable` · `load-failed` · `not-built`, never a refusal; its held handles live until `spawn_child` returns) → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: the bounded `--version` read logged as a `version-probe` `process-start`/`process-exit` pair, the stamps read, `cli_version`/`cli_verified` carried into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; `run` prints nothing on any gate outcome) → endpoint bind → the budget gate at start (span `run.budget_eval` with `trigger: start`; it reads `budget.json`, restores no override and writes nothing; the thresholds were read from `config.json` earlier in the start, each rejection logged then) → first snapshot (its `budget_paused` is that verdict, its `budget_override_until` always absent) → heartbeat → start events (record two, `budget-gate`, carries that verdict's `data`, where it carried the constant `{"paused": false}` before chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) → spawn, so the child's first SessionStart hook finds a listening endpoint and a recorded snapshot. Since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the start also restores the wrapper's link set before the endpoint serves: it reads `events.ndjson` twice there (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`), the first snapshot's `links` is the restored set, the start appends no line for links and its start records are unchanged. `viola revive` starts through the same function, so a revived start's first snapshot carries the logged links.
 A gone instance's directory is reused at once, and its `events.ndjson` is appended to, never truncated.

subject: dec-error-handling
text: - **[Error Handling] thiserror 2.0.20, one enum per workspace crate (one ratified exception: `viola-pty`'s `PtyError` has a hand-written `Display`/`Error` with fixed messages, because the seam's normal dependencies are exactly portable-pty, tracing, windows-sys and libc; portable-pty's anyhow error is kept only as a boxed source. `viola-agent-claude`'s `AgentError` sits at the crate root and holds the stamps envelope's `StampsMalformed` beside the hook payload's `Malformed` — the second enum `StampError` was folded into it by chunk 2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness. One open divergence, not an exception: the crate also holds the thiserror enum `Refusal` (`BatchScriptChild`, `NotFound`, the `resolve_program` refusal), which predates that fold; the rule stands, and its fold or ratification is open). A second open divergence, not an exception: `viola-mcp` holds `ServeError` (`Runtime`, `Initialize`, `Session`; fixed messages, returned by `serve`) beside `McpError` (`Internal`, Display `internal error`) (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); the rule stands, and its fold or ratification is open; anyhow 1.0.104 only in the `viola` bin: its `main`, dispatch (`cmd::dispatch` returns the error with the resolved home and instance) and the catch-site reporter `viola::obs::report_internal_error`.** `RefusalReason` lives in `viola-core`. Rationale: callers branch on refusal variants across three surfaces (channel, CLI exit codes, MCP `isError`). anyhow's context chains are only useful where a person reads them: the owner's post-mortem, which gets the chain as `chain` in `instances/<name>/diagnostics/detail-<role>.ndjson`, never a role line, stdout or stderr.

subject: dec-module-boundaries
text: - **[Module Boundaries] Cargo workspace, flat `crates/` layout, with the root `Cargo.toml` as both the `viola` bin package and `[workspace]`.** Members: `viola-core`, `viola-pty`, `viola-channel`, `viola-state`, `viola-agent-claude`, `viola-mcp`, plus the test-only `viola-e2e` (the `viola-harness` agent-run harness; no product crate depends on it). Each product crate is created by the first chunk that consumes it. `fuzz/` (the `viola-fuzz` cargo-fuzz targets) is NOT a member. It is its own cargo workspace, excluded by the root's `exclude = ["fuzz"]`, so its nightly toolchain and C++-building libfuzzer-sys never enter the root graph. Among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables `tokio` (`rt`); `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (`["dep:tokio", "interprocess/tokio"]`, the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables and, in a package-scoped test build, the channel's own test-only `fake-agent = ["tokio"]` (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers); the test-only `viola-e2e` takes `rt` + `process`. No other product member's normal graph reaches tokio (the sole-root loop and `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh`). Rationale: the compiler enforces that `viola-pty` cannot see `viola-agent-claude`. `cargo install --path .` requires the bin at the root. cargo_pup needs nightly and was rejected.

subject: dec-deployment-distribution
text:
- **[Deployment / Distribution] `cargo install --path .`, with the plugin compiled into the binary (KEYSTONE).** `hooks/hooks.json`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` are embedded via `include_str!`, and `plugin.json`'s version comes from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. At start, `viola run` copies its own exe to `<viola home>/bin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/viola(.exe)` if that copy is absent, and re-hashes an existing copy before reusing it: a copy that no longer matches refuses the start (exit 1, `pinned-hash-mismatch`) and is left as found. On Windows x64 the binary also embeds Microsoft's ConPTY companions (`src/conpty.rs`: `include_bytes!` of `vendor/conpty/<version>/x64/{OpenConsole.exe,conpty.dll}`; the package version, the nupkg SHA-256 and the two file SHA-256s have that file's text as their one home) and writes them write-if-absent to `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` (`viola_state::pin::pin_companions`; never overwritten). At every start each companion is opened with `FILE_SHARE_READ` only and re-hashed in full against its pin, and the handles are held until the spawn. Unlike the exe, a mismatched companion never refuses the start: it is left as found, never loaded, and the child runs on the inbox ConPTY ([PTY]). The subdirectory, not the pinned dir itself, because the pinned dir is first on the child's PATH. The first start of a version writes the two files (1 176 216 B); as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty on the dev host under a parallel test suite, `pin_companions` took a median 1 193 ms there (each write ~0.55 s), while CI's perf and test jobs stayed green (ci#36566391084) — the root tests seed their homes with the companions instead (test-plan §5), and no bound was raised.
 It rewrites the plugin files on every start to `<viola home>/plugin/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>-<short content hash>/` and substitutes the copy's path (forward slashes) into every exec-form `command` in `hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`. It then passes that folder with `--plugin-dir`, sets `VIOLA_BIN` to the copy and puts the copy's folder first on the child's PATH. `hooks.json` registers seven exec-form entries, each `"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@"` (substituted at start) with `"args": ["hook", "<kebab event>"]`: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop with `"timeout": 5`; SessionEnd with no `timeout` key; Notification, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure with `"async": true`. The dialog tier joins them (chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id): PreToolUse with `"matcher": "AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode"` and PermissionRequest, each with `"timeout": 3615` — nine exec-form entries in all. `.mcp.json` registers the server `viola` as `{"mcpServers": {"viola": {"command": "@@VIOLA_BIN@@", "args": ["mcp"]}}}`, the pinned copy's absolute path substituted at every start (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers; until the `mcp` verb existed it shipped `{"mcpServers": {}}`, on the operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan that a registered command that exits 2 would block Claude Code). A registered `viola mcp` that exits 1 (its home refused by `home_passes`) does not block the CLI's start: the session reaches `idle` and the CLI logs that server's connection as failed (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings/evidence/live-round.md`; its Windows leg owed to "Windows-only live measurements"). Hooks and MCP never search PATH. Rationale: the binary and the plugin can no longer drift apart. The prototype proved that PATH-found hooks run a different binary from the wrapper after a rebuild.
 The content hash is part of the key because `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` stays `0.1.0` across development rebuilds, so the version alone would collide. A rebuild therefore never changes what a running session calls. Known trade-off: a hook fix applies only to sessions started after the rebuild. The per-frame `v` + sender version stays as the second safety net, for the optional user-level install (`viola plugin install`), which is not bound to a wrapper's pinned copy.

subject: dec-plugin-scope
text:
- **[Plugin Scope] The plugin loads only into wrapped sessions via `--plugin-dir`.** Both driver and driven run under `viola run`. `viola plugin install` (a local marketplace) is optional, for the MCP verbs in an unwrapped driver. The installed plugin carries only `.mcp.json` and no hooks, so a wrapped session that also has it installed never runs two hook processes for one event (two `hook.dialog` requests for one dialog). Its `command` is the absolute path of the exe that ran `plugin install`, never a PATH lookup: as built, `viola plugin install` writes only `<home>/marketplace/` and spawns no `claude`, and its `.mcp.json` registers `viola` as `{"command": <the canonical current_exe, forward slashes>, "args": ["--home", <the canonical home, forward slashes>, "mcp"]}`, each document built by `serde_json` (`viola_agent_claude::marketplace::marketplace_files`). A wrapped session that also has the installed plugin enabled starts one `viola` MCP server, the `--plugin-dir` plugin's, and that server answers its tools: the installed plugin's `viola mcp` never starts there, and the session runs one SessionStart hook process (as measured on claude 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-18-plugin-precedence-live-readings/evidence/live-round.md`: the wrapped home's `mcp.ndjson` one `process-start{subject:"self"}` and the `list` call's `agents-probe` pair, the installed home none, the CLI's MCP log one server). It is no capability-ledger row (no `send` relies on it, the ruled limit); its Windows leg is owed to "Windows-only live measurements". Rationale: unwrapped sessions carry no viola hooks at all, so there is no per-tool-call spawn cost outside viola. The exceptions are `viola verify`'s transient unwrapped children, all gone when verify ends.
 The first is the print-mode probe, an unwrapped `claude -p` that loads only the `viola-verify-probe` plugin (four exec-form `hook <event> --capture` hooks) from `ledger/probes/<pid>/plugin/`. The other five are the interactive runs: Run A, untrusted in an OS-temp `viola-verify-*` dir and killed at its screen; Run B, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`; Runs C and D, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/` and `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/`, each loading the dialog-kind `viola-verify-probe` plugin; and Run E, trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/`, loading the capture plugin from `ledger/probes/<pid>/resume/plugin/` and resuming Run B's first session with `--resume <id>`, no key typed. Runs B, C and D, as real interactive turns, also run the user's own global hooks, and Runs C and D, and Run B on Windows, the user's own status line (on Unix Run B's status line is the probe capture its one probe `--settings` names, [CLI Version Compatibility]), and each leaves the CLI's session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/` (an accepted residual, security-plan Data Protection): Run B three per real-CLI verify, its session, the `<id>-backup-<n>.jsonl` the CLI writes at its pasted `/compact`'s compaction and the session its pasted `/clear` opens (the last inferred, not read), and C and D one each; Run E adds none (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, `evidence/live-round.md`: the `viola-verify` transcript count 60 → 65). The print-mode probe leaves the CLI's empty project dir for its cwd `ledger/probes/<pid>/` under `~/.claude/projects/` (a `memory/` dir, no transcript), the same accepted residual (as measured on 2.1.296 and 2.1.302 on the Linux dev host at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola/evidence/switch-round.md`).

subject: dec-cli-conventions
text: - **[CLI Conventions] Human text by default, `--json` for agents, a typed exit code per refusal. Prompt text comes from stdin or `--file`, never from a leading-slash argument.** viola warns when an argument carries a Git Bash rewritten-path prefix. Rationale: Git Bash rewrites `/skill` arguments into Windows paths (brief §6), and agents need machine-parseable refusals. `viola revive` takes `--json` on both arms (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): a refused strict-modes check or a preflight refusal prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`) in place of its `unable:` / `hint:` pair, exit 1, and `<name> --list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order; without `--json` the pairs and the `--list` rows are byte-identical. A refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight (`batch-script-child`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `squatted-name`, a `claude` not on `PATH` as `internal-error`) prints no document as landed; its document is owed to the working-route entry "Exit-cause code catalogue".
